findings.title: robots.txt returned HTTP 404
findings.should_be: robots.txt should return HTTP 200 with valid directives.
findings.fix: Ensure /robots.txt is served correctly. If you don't have one, create a minimal robots.txt that allows AI bots (see the fix below).

findings.title: sitemap.xml is missing or unreachable
findings.should_be: A valid sitemap.xml listing your key pages.
findings.fix:
Create a sitemap.xml at the site root. If you use a CMS (WordPress, Shopify, Webflow), there's usually a plugin or built-in feature to generate one. Reference it in robots.txt:

Sitemap: https://yoursite.com/sitemap.xml

findings.title: No structured data (schema.org JSON-LD) on homepage
findings.evidence: No <script type='application/ld+json'> tags were found in the page HTML.
findings.should_be: At minimum, Organization and WebSite schema should be present.
findings.fix:
Add this to your homepage <head> (replace the placeholders):

<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Organization",
  "name": "Your Business Name",
  "url": "https://yoursite.com",
  "logo": "https://yoursite.com/logo.png",
  "description": "One sentence describing what your business does.",
  "sameAs": [
    "https://twitter.com/yourhandle",
    "https://www.linkedin.com/company/yourcompany",
    "https://www.crunchbase.com/organization/yourcompany"
  ]
}
</script>

Tip: if you use WordPress, plugins like Yoast SEO or RankMath can generate this automatically. If you use Webflow, it's under Page Settings > Schema Markup.

findings.title: Missing meta description on homepage
findings.should_be: A meta description of 120-160 characters summarizing the page.
findings.fix:
Add a meta description:

<meta name="description" content="Your one-sentence value proposition. What you do, who you serve, and why it matters (120-160 characters)">

findings.title: Few or no <h2> subheadings
findings.evidence: Found 0 H2 tags. Subheadings help structure content for readability and machine understanding.
findings.should_be: Use H2 subheadings to break up content sections.
findings.fix: Add <h2> subheadings to organize your content into clear sections.

findings.title: Very little text content on homepage
findings.evidence: Only 2 paragraph(s) found. Word count: 19. AI engines need text to extract and cite.
findings.should_be: Substantive text content (300+ words) that answers visitor questions.
findings.fix: Add descriptive text content that explains what you do, who you serve, and answers common questions. Aim for at least 300 words of relevant content.

findings.title: Missing Open Graph tags
findings.evidence: No og:title or og:description tags found. Open Graph tags control how your page appears when shared on social media and some AI platforms.
findings.fix:
Add Open Graph tags:

<meta property="og:title" content="Your Title">
<meta property="og:description" content="Your description">
<meta property="og:image" content="https://yoursite.com/og-image.png">
<meta property="og:url" content="https://yoursite.com">

findings.title: Missing canonical URL tag
findings.evidence: No <link rel='canonical'> tag found. Canonical tags prevent duplicate content issues by telling search engines which URL is the 'master' version of a page.
findings.fix:
Add a canonical tag:

<link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/">
